business_scope.primary_industry_name: General Partner Management Entity for Early-Stage Technology Funds

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Marshall Islands (Unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state tax or incorporation distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid legal system based on Common Law statutory principles; corporate code modelled on the Delaware General Corporation Law and the revised Model Business Corporation Act; customary law reserved for land and traditional rights matters
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Compact of Free Association between the Republic of the Marshall Islands and the United States of America (1986; Amended Compact 2003/2023) — economic, trade and investment provisions with US MFN and national-treatment standards
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (PACER Plus; signed 2017, entered into force 2020 for RMI) — trade-in-services and investment-related disciplines
US–RMI Model 1 Intergovernmental Agreement under FATCA (2013) — bilateral tax information exchange arrangement
No general network of standalone BITs or DTAAs is currently in force for the Marshall Islands

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Constitution of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (1979); Business Corporations Act 1990 (BCCA), Title 8 of the Marshall Islands Revised Code, as amended (name clearance in BCCA §§ 8–9; registered office and registered agent requirements; mandatory beneficial-ownership filing provisions); Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Act 2018 (AMLCFTA) and the AMLCFTA (General) Regulations 2019; Registered Agents Act 2014, as amended; Financial Intelligence Unit directives on UBO records, customer due diligence and PEPs; FATF Recommendations 10, 22 and 25 and the Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering (APG) mutual evaluation framework applicable to the RMI
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (confidential UBO return filed with the Registrar of Corporations and accessible to the RMI FIU and designated domestic regulators; no public search of beneficial owners is available)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the Articles of Incorporation (proposed or filed)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro (or licensed Registered Agent's certified copy)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization — the RMI is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention; chain authentication required: notarisation in jurisdiction of origin, then in the US the Department of State Authentication Office, then legalization by the Embassy of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, Washington D.C.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Fact / Certificate of Good Standing (name clearance and incorporation confirmation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization via the same chain-authentication path (RMI not an Apostille contracting state)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency and Register of Directors/Officers with UBO declaration schedule
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Registered Agent (authorized under the RMI Registered Agents Act 2014)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization via the chain-authentication path described above

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passports, proof of address and source-of-funds declarations of each UBO / general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public licensed in the UBO's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (origin notary certification, then US DOS Authentication where applicable, then RMI Consulate legalization)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference and professional referee letters for the VC GP / proposed fund account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Original issuing licensed bank or statutory professional body
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization or bank-to-bank SWIFT authenticated confirmation accepted at correspondent's discretion

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of every UBO, director, officer, GP partner and authorised signatory against (i) the RMI FIU consolidated domestic designations, (ii) the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, (iii) the US OFAC SDN / SSI / non-SDN lists — de facto required for USD correspondent banking access, (iv) UK OFSI and EU consolidated lists. PEP detection follows FATF-style categories (state, judicial and military officials, SOE executives, senior political-party figures, plus close associates and first-degree relatives); any positive hit requires enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval and source-of-wealth verification. Sanctions hits trigger an immediate 24-hour asset freeze hold and a Suspicious Transaction Report to the RMI FIU within 3 business days. Covered persons are re-screened at least every 90 days.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RMI Corporate Registry — Online Name Search and Reservation Portal (Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Ministry of Finance, Majuro; accessible via licensed registered agents and the e-services module)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All corporate names must be expressed in the Latin (Roman) alphabet; English is the official corporate language. Marshallese diacritics are tolerated; names in non-Latin scripts (CJK, Cyrillic, Arabic) must be transliterated into Roman characters and verified for phonetic collision against the registry. The name must include a corporate suffix ('Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Limited' or abbreviations 'Corp.', 'Inc.', 'Ltd.'; 'Company'/'Co.' permitted). Names must not be identical or confusingly similar to existing registered marks under the BCCA § 8 standard.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Step 1 — within 14 days of a written rejection, file a reconsideration request with the Registrar citing distinguishing elements (extra words, geographic qualifiers, approved suffix, unique mark) and, where relevant, a notarized consent/waiver letter from the earlier-name holder. Step 2 — the Registrar must respond within 10 working days; a second rejection must be justified in writing against BCCA § 9 grounds. Step 3 — administrative appeal to the Minister of Finance within 30 days of the final refusal, or judicial review to the High Court of the Marshall Islands (Civil Division) within 30 days of exhaustion of administrative remedies. Filing fee: approximately US$50 for the administrative appeal and US$250 for High Court filing. A name reservation may be extended for an additional 30 days at the Registrar's discretion upon written application before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted — the BCCA requires a registered office and a licensed registered agent in the RMI; a non-resident, tax-exempt venture-capital GP may maintain only the agent's address in Majuro as its statutory seat and operate entirely outside the RMI. A fully virtual footprint (no local staff or premises) is compliant for this industry, provided the registered agent maintains the statutory registers and accepts service of process at the registered office. No in-country economic substance is currently required for non-resident corporations, although substance benchmarking for the GP's jurisdiction of management may apply to the underlying fund for US federal income-tax purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for standard non-resident entities — estimated 2% annual probability of unannounced on-site inspection of the registered agent's premises; increases to 10–15% following FIU trigger events (sanctions alerts, adverse media, repeated high-risk cash flows or AML/CFT inspection cycle targets). Inspections are conducted jointly by the Registrar and the FIU at the registered agent's Majuro office, not at the entity's foreign operational premises.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate name clearance search and priority reservation (counter-search against BCCA § 8 prohibited and confusing-similarity index)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Ministry of Finance, Majuro
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff — Registrar's published fee schedule (reservation US$50 plus search and courier handling approximately US$25)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Filing fee for Articles of Incorporation (non-resident Business Corporation; authorised capital up to US$50,000)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff — BCCA / Registrar's published fee schedule (tiered by authorised capital)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: First-year advance franchise tax / annual report fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff — minimum franchise tax for authorised capital up to US$50,000

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization bundle for UBO declarations, passport copies, incumbency certificate and governance resolutions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary Public licensed in the origin jurisdiction of UBOs / general partners
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark — per-document notarial fees in major financial centers, estimated at US$25–50 per certificate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consular legalization chain (US Department of State Authentication Office plus Embassy of the Republic of the Marshall Islands certification of 3–4 corporate documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: US Department of State, Washington D.C.; Embassy of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, Washington D.C.
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing government fee scale and courier/agency market benchmark (RMI not an Apostille state; chain authentication required)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Licensed Registered Agent retainer and statutory registered-office provision (Majuro, 12 months)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Fully licensed RMI Registered Agent (authorized under the Registered Agents Act 2014)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark — leading RMI agents quote US$700–1,000 per annum for registered office, registered agent and statutory mail holding

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO piercing, PEP / OFAC / UN sanctions screening and adverse-media analysis for all GBP identities and indirect ownership chains
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External compliance counsel / law firm engaged for pre-incorporation due diligence
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark — per-subject screening packages in offshore corporate practice, estimated at US$40–80 per principal

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT programme design for the VC GP: FIU registration filing, risk assessment, internal controls manual and SAR-flagging procedures (first year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compliance counsel plus RMI Financial Intelligence Unit registration (no separate FIU levy)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark — small financial-institution AML manual and onboarding package

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act 1990 (B.C.A.), Republic of the Marshall Islands, as amended — ss. 16-30 (formation and Articles of Incorporation), ss. 47-54 (directors and officers), ss. 92-96 (registered office and registered agent)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Business Entities Division, Office of the Attorney General, Republic of the Marshall Islands
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form BC-INC/01), together with the Name Clearance Certificate and Registered Agent Consent
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The B.C.A. imposes no statutory minimum paid-up capital; the corporation may issue par or no-par shares, including capital-call subscription commitments, and consideration must equal at least par value (where applicable); no escrow account or capital deposit rule applies to non-resident business corporations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation accepts the initial share subscriptions and authorizes issuance of shares for lawful consideration of not less than par value, with unpaid commitments reflected as capital calls. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office and licensed registered agent in the Marshall Islands be adopted at the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the persons named in Schedule A are elected directors. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] is appointed Chief Executive Officer, [Name] Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] Corporate Secretary. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the officers are empowered to execute subscription agreements, open capital-call and escrow accounts, and complete filings necessary to conduct venture capital fund activities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Business Entities Division, Office of the Attorney General, Republic of the Marshall Islands (via e-Registry portal or licensed registered agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name clearance request for the proposed corporate name; verify its uniqueness against the registry index; pay the statutory name reservation fee; the name must include 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Company', or an authorized abbreviation.
required_dossiers: Fee payment receipt for name reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity or confusion, submit an alternate name, provide written consent from the conflicting entity, or appeal to the Registrar for an administrative review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of Licensed Registered Agent and Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Attorney General, Registered Agents Division, Republic of the Marshall Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Marshall Islands licensed registered agent and confirm the physical registered office address; obtain the agent's executed written consent; the registered office must be maintained at a physical street address within the Republic of the Marshall Islands.
required_dossiers: Registered agent consent and acceptance form
Copy of the registered agent license
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the chosen agent is unlicensed or its license has lapsed, promptly appoint a substitute licensed agent and file the corresponding change of registered agent prior to filing the Articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator or authorized filing agent on behalf of the Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation stating the corporate name, purpose clause covering venture capital fund management and general partner services, authorized share capital, registered agent particulars, and incorporator details; execute the Articles with notarization where required by the B.C.A. and the filing manual.
required_dossiers: Signed and notarized Articles of Incorporation
Power of attorney (if executed through an agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the draft is defective, amend the affected provisions and re-execute; ministerial or clerical errors may be cured by filing Articles of Correction after registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing and Statutory Registration of the Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Business Entities Division, Office of the Attorney General, Republic of the Marshall Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Articles of Incorporation to the Registrar by courier or the e-Registry portal together with the prescribed filing fee; upon acceptance, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation; pay the initial registration and annual maintenance fees.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a deficiency query, respond within the stated cure period by filing corrected documents, supplementary sworn statements, or verified explanations; failure to cure may result in withdrawal, which is avoidable by timely resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Bylaws and First Organizational Board Actions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold an organizational meeting or act by unanimous written consent; adopt the corporate bylaws; approve the First Board Resolution; create the share ledger and issue certificates to initial shareholders; designate an AML compliance officer to satisfy the Medium-Risk Enhanced AML/CFT obligations applicable to venture capital general partners.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution or unanimous written consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Procedural or quorum defects may be cured by a subsequent board ratification resolution adopted by the current directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations and Marshall Islands Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a Certificate of Good Standing from the Registrar; register the AML/CFT compliance program with the FIU; open the capital-call and escrow accounts at a licensed bank using the corporate KYC dossier; file the beneficial ownership information with the registered agent and maintain it current.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If FIU or banking onboarding is delayed, provide the filing receipt and corporate authorization to the financial institution, seek conditional onboarding, and escalate to the licensed registered agent for procedural acceleration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Marshall Islands Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) in coordination with the Banking Commissioner and the Registrar of Non-Resident Entities
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Non-Resident Financial Services Operating Registration and AML/CFT Compliance Certificate (General Partner / Venture Capital Fund Management)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Marshall Islands Environmental Protection Authority (RMI EPA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category IV – Exempt Administrative Use / Registration only (office-based financial services; no industrial activity or point-source discharge)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater discharge or point-source air emissions; office waste handled under municipal collection standards; RMI EPA registration applies only if hazardous waste generation exceeds 100 kg per calendar year; otherwise exempt.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the RMI Fire Safety Inspector for the registered office premises; structural load inspection certificate for office and records storage areas; occupational health and workplace clearance covering ventilation, egress, and emergency lighting; annual municipal business premises inspection.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Republic of the Marshall Islands Ministry of Finance, Banking and Postal Services, Revenue Management Division (Majuro); corporate registration and annual franchise tax administered by the Office of the Registrar of Corporations (Majuro) under the Business Corporations Act 1990. No national digital tax portal exists; filings are submitted through licensed registered agents in paper or PDF form.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned non-resident Business Corporation (NRDC) files Articles of Incorporation with the Office of the Registrar of Corporations through a licensed registered agent. The Registrar issues a Certificate of Incorporation bearing the corporate registration number; the RMI does not issue a TIN or VAT ID for offshore exempt entities. The Certificate of Incorporation and subsequent Certificate of Good Standing serve as the authority's proof of tax-exempt status. A TIN and Business License are required only if the entity engages in economic activity within the RMI, in which case it must register with the Revenue Management Division for the 3% gross revenue tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box, hybrid mismatch, or elective taxation regime exists under Marshall Islands law; the exemption of non-resident domestic corporations from RMI income and gross revenue tax is mandatory and automatic, not elective. A US owner may file US Form 8832 for US federal classification purposes, but such an election has no effect on the entity's RMI tax status.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT/GST/Sales and Use Tax in force. The RMI indirect revenue regime consists of customs import duties under the Customs Act 1990 and a 3% Gross Revenue Tax under the Income Tax Act 1989, both of which apply only to persons or goods with an RMI territorial nexus.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable - no VAT/GST legislation exists. For the 3% Gross Revenue Tax, any entity 'carrying on business' inside the RMI is liable from the first US dollar of locally sourced gross revenue; no minimum threshold is provided. A non-resident venture capital GP with no RMI office, employees, or local revenue never triggers registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. The RMI imposes no electronic invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, API integration, or digital stamping mandate. Paper-based invoicing and customs declarations remain the operative standard.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable in a VAT sense because the RMI imposes no VAT/GST on goods or services. Management fees and carried interest derived by a non-resident GP from offshore venture funds are outside the RMI tax net entirely and therefore do not require a zero-rating mechanism. Where physical goods are exported from RMI territory, customs duty exemption or rebate may be claimed under the Customs Act 1990 for temporarily imported or re-exported goods; no VAT refund mechanism exists.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The RMI has no export-VAT refund fraud regime because no VAT is levied. General fraud and misrepresentation provisions in the Business Corporations Act 1990 and the Customs Act 1990 empower the Registrar and customs authorities to impose fines, seize goods, order forfeiture, and dissolve the offending corporation for false statements or duty evasion. A non-resident entity that misrepresents its status or activities to the Registrar to retain automatic tax exemption risks revocation of its registration and loss of separate legal personality, exposing owners to retrospective personal liability.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banking Commission of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (Banking Commissioner, Ministry of Finance), established under the Banking Act 1994. The Marshall Islands has no domestic central bank, no monetary policy authority, and no foreign exchange administration; the lawful tender is the United States dollar, distributed through the U.S. Federal Reserve correspondent network.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility in both law and practice. Because the RMI issues no domestic currency and the U.S. dollar is legal tender, the distinction between current-account and capital-account convertibility is effectively immaterial: no Marshall Islands statute restricts the purchase, sale, repatriation, or liquidation of foreign exchange. The RMI is an IMF member state (membership effective 21 May 1992) and its exchange arrangements are consistent with Article VIII obligations, with no restrictions on payments and transfers for current international transactions. A non-resident Business Corporation acting as a venture capital General Partner faces zero statutory profit-remittance hurdles; the only practical impediments arise from U.S. correspondent-bank sanction screening and global AML/CFT de-risking, not from Marshall Islands law.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. The RMI imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender period, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation requirement under the Banking Act 1994 or any exchange-control decree. All export receipts, capital-call inflows, carried interest, and management fee receivables may be freely retained and disposed of in USD without central-bank approval, escrow, or conversion obligation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility with strict legal constraints. Offshore digital EMI accounts are not licensed by the RMI Banking Commissioner and have no supervisory standing in the Marshall Islands. US/UK-licensed EMIs will generally accept RMI-registered corporations only after enhanced due diligence, and several major EMIs systematically decline RMI entities because of the jurisdiction's elevated AML/CFT risk profile and correspondent-bank de-risking. EMIs may serve as auxiliary disbursement rails but cannot substitute for a regulated Tier-1 bank account for capital calls or carried interest.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance is not a statutory mandate in the Banking Act 1994, but RMI-licensed banks apply an internal expectation that at least one natural-person director or the ultimate beneficial owner attends an in-person interview at the Majuro branch, reflecting the enhanced-risk classification of a non-resident VC General Partner. Remote opening is occasionally permitted for existing customers and for branches of U.S.-chartered banks, using notarized and apostilled corporate documents, live video identification, and a licensed RMI registered agent; however, pure remote onboarding without a prior banking relationship is rarely approved for Medium_Risk_Enhanced structures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident corporation underwriting an omnibus venture fund with undisclosed LP investors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum and Articles/Bylaws, register of directors and shareholders, licensed registered-agent consent letter, complete fund-structure diagram, executed Limited Partnership Agreement, certified beneficial-ownership declaration, and the RMI tax-exemption or non-resident status certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex inbound capital-call wires from many unrelated investors triggering structuring/smurfing red flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: LP subscription agreements, capital call notices with unique reference identifiers, management-committee minutes authorizing each call, investor KYC/CDD files (passport, proof of domicile, source of wealth), OFAC/PEP screening results, and a reconciliation ledger matching each MT103 field-70 reference to the capital call schedule.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Jurisdiction-risk concern arising from the RMI's prior inclusion in AML/CFT or EU tax listings
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Banking Commission licensing status, APG/FATF engagement narrative, corporate registry extract evidencing good standing, audited GP financial statements, the GP's AML/CFT compliance manual compliant with the Banking Act 1994 and the Counter-Terrorism and Transnational Organized Crime Act 2004, and an external legal opinion on the structure's tax transparency.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital calls are settled by SWIFT MT103 wires from each LP's bank into the GP's Capital Escrow Account, with USD clearing occurring through the U.S. correspondent-bank network (Fedwire and CHIPS). Each instruction must populate field 50 with the LP legal name, field 59 with the account beneficiary, and field 70 with the fund identifier, capital call number, and investor reference; where the originating jurisdiction applies standardized economic-purpose codes, the flow is classified as 'S3010 — Investment in equity capital' under the IMF BPM6 purpose-code framework. No RMI exchange-control filing, central-bank approval, or declaration is required. Value release is conditional on positive matching against the capital call schedule, the subscription agreement, and the investor KYC pack, followed by an OFAC/UN/EU sanctions screen at the receiving bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Portfolio-company investments and drawdown disbursements are executed by SWIFT MT103 corporate credits bearing the investment-agreement reference and the payment purpose 'Equity Investment', 'Convertible Note', or 'Working Capital Facility' in field 70. Irrevocable documentary credits governed by UCP600 are available through the issuing bank for trade-linked transactions but are non-standard for venture-stage technology funding. All outbound disbursements are cleared via the same USD correspondent rails, screened against OFAC, EU, UN, and UK sanctions lists, and recorded against the fund's cash-flow model. The RMI imposes no capital-export licence, exchange permit, or reporting obligation on outbound USD transfers.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts on liquid pairs (EUR/USD, GBP/USD, JPY/USD, AUD/USD) covering portfolio-company expenses and re-investment needs
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or illiquid emerging-market currencies encountered in follow-on venture rounds
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps on dual-currency bridge facilities between the GP's holding entities and portfolio companies
Vanilla FX options for capped-cost hedging of committed-capital drawdowns in foreign currency

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Report (Form A) with franchise tax computation and resolution confirming no changes or listing amendments
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing window opens January 1; final due date is April 30 of each calendar year, regardless of incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing between May 1 and May 31 incurs USD 100 late penalty; filings after May 31 incur USD 200 penalty; failure to file for two consecutive years triggers administrative dissolution and loss of limited liability protection

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent Confirmation and Entity Status Certificate renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Agent licensed by the Marshall Islands Registrar of Corporations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Concurrently with the April 30 annual report deadline; agent must within 30 days notify Registrar of any change in registered office or registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a qualified Marshall Islands registered agent and registered office on file results in immediate administrative dissolution and disqualification from transacting business

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Franchise Tax Settlement and Economic Substance / Exempt-Status Declaration for Non-Resident Business Corporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations and Department of Taxation on delegated collection basis
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same April 30 annual deadline; no separate tax return required for non-resident, tax-exempt business corporations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid franchise tax bears interest at 1.5% per month; continued non-payment after 90 days leads to certificate of dissolution and automatic revocation of exempt-status privileges

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory statutory audit for a non-resident, non-public Marshall Islands Business Corporation under the Business Corporations Act; an audit becomes mandatory only if (i) the corporation is licensed under the Marshall Islands Investment Business Act or equivalent financial services license, (ii) shareholders representing at least 10% of voting shares file an audit demand, or (iii) the Articles of Incorporation expressly require audited financial statements
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No statutorily mandated accounting standard for exempt non-resident corporations; IFRS or US GAAP may be adopted voluntarily, and audited capital-call fund financial statements for venture capital investors are customarily prepared under US GAAP or IFRS

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual public UBO confirmation filing is required by the Marshall Islands Registry; annual report may confirm shareholder and director details, but beneficial ownership information is maintained confidentially by the registered agent and the corporation's records, and is disclosed only pursuant to a lawful court order, criminal investigation, or explicit statutory demand, including any share transfer effectuated during the previous year
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Directors' and Shareholders' Resolutions
Register of Transfers and Share Transfer Ledger

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 850 – USD 1,500 per annum through a licensed Marshall Islands registered agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not statutorily required; investor-requested venture capital GP audit typically ranges from USD 8,000 – USD 20,000 depending on transaction volume and consolidated SPV count

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Non-resident Business Corporations are exempt from Marshall Islands income tax on all income derived outside the Republic; no capital gains tax; no payroll tax; no social security contributions for non-resident employees; no withholding tax on dividends, interest, royalties, or management fees paid to non-residents; no gross receipts tax; annual flat government franchise tax based on authorized capital structure

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Marshall Islands Business Corporation Annual Report and Franchise Tax Return (Form BC-AR) filed via the Marshall Islands Registered Agent's online portal or through the Registrar of Corporations' e-filing system
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annually on the last business day of the calendar month preceding the anniversary of incorporation; if the anniversary falls in the final quarter, the deadline is extended to the last business day of the following month

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity legal name as shown on the Certificate of Incorporation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the full registered English legal name; transliterations are not accepted

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered agent name and registered office address in the Marshall Islands
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be the licensed Marshall Islands registered agent; PO boxes are not permitted unless accompanied by a physical street location

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorized share capital and class structure
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the aggregate authorized capital in United States dollars and the number of authorized shares by class
List at least one director of any nationality; no residency requirement, but a full residential address must be supplied for each individual
Describe the venture capital general partner management activity, including investment management, capital calls, and fee income
Use the statutory franchise tax schedule based on authorized capital; the minimum is US$200 and the maximum is US$350, unless the corporation holds an international banking or insurance license

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certification of non-resident status and extraterritorial income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Certify that no income was derived from sources within the Marshall Islands and that all commercial activity occurred outside the Republic
The Marshall Islands registered agent must sign and certify the filing; director signatures are normally not required on the annual report

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filed annual reports incur a penalty of 10% of the franchise tax due; failure to file for two consecutive years may trigger involuntary dissolution by the Registrar; reinstatement after dissolution requires payment of all arrears, penalties, and a reinstatement filing fee plus 10% penalty on the total amount as provided under the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Marshall Islands does not maintain a comprehensive double taxation agreement network; non-resident shareholders are not subject to any withholding tax on distributions because no domestic withholding tax is imposed, so no treaty relief procedure, TRC submission, or teletax clearance protocol is required; a shareholder of record may obtain a mere certificate of tax-exempt status from the Registrar upon request to evidence the 0% domestic tax position
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Marshall Islands statutory withholding tax on cross-border royalties and interest is 0%; because the DTA network is essentially negligible, the effective rate is 0% on both IP royalty payments and debt interest paid by a non-resident Business Corporation

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: The Marshall Islands does not have a statutory transfer pricing regime and does not impose Local File, Master File, or Country-by-Country reporting thresholds in USD; however, venture capital general partner entities are deemed to require a contemporaneous transfer pricing policy if they are part of a multinational group whose ultimate parent files CbC reports in any OECD/G20 jurisdiction and whose group revenue exceeds the equivalent of the OECD threshold (EUR 750 million / approximately USD 810 million)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Marshall Islands has adopted a Non-Resident Domestic Corporation economic substance framework aligned with the 2019 EU Code of Conduct Group requirements; in-scope entities (including Pure Equity Holding Companies, finance and leasing companies, and holding companies that generate income from geographically mobile activities such as management or investment services) must satisfy the Economic Substance Regulations and maintain the following evidenced in the Marshall Islands or utility-certified documentation: (a) locally managed meetings by at least one executive, (b) adequate physical presence including a lease or owned premises, (c) a dedicated bank account and books of account, and (d) an annual economic substance return filed with the Registrar within seven months of the fiscal year-end

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A non-resident Business Corporation holding a venture capital fund general partner function that files an annual report with 0% franchise tax, maintains no Marshall Islands footprint, conducts no board meetings, has no physical presence, and fails to file the annual Economic Substance Return, while claiming a pure holding and management fee exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Pursuant to the Marshall Islands Economic Substance Regulations, the Registrar may impose administrative fines of up to US$100,000 for failure to file the economic substance return or misrepresentation; equivalent fixed penalties apply for each year of non-compliance; the Registrar may also strike the company from the register, dissolve the entity, and issue a certificate of dissolution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers knowingly causing or permitting the filing of false economic substance declarations face individual fines of up to US$20,000 per offense, civil damages for any resulting tax loss, and disqualification from serving as a director in the Marshall Islands; if continued registration is maintained through false sworn declarations, the corporate veil will be pierced to hold directors jointly and severally liable for the company's unpaid franchise taxes, penalties, and restoration costs.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Veil Piercing / Fraudulent Transfer of Fund Assets
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The venture capital general partner uses its Marshall Islands vehicle to receive carried interest and management fees, then distributes profits to foreign principals while disregarding entity formalities by commingling investor capital, funding personal expenses, issuing false capital calls, or operating with grossly inadequate capitalization.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under general principles of Marshall Islands law derived from the Business Corporations Act, courts will disregard limited liability upon a finding of sham or alter ego; penalties include the entry of judgment against shareholders and principals for all amounts paid out of the deficient entity, punitive damages, and disgorgement of fees; the Registrar may likewise dissolve the corporation administratively for failing to maintain a registered agent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who authorize fraudulent distributions or who are found to be the alter ego of the venture capital fund may be personally and jointly liable to fund investors and general creditors for the full amount of distributions made while insolvent; travel restrictions and cancellation of the entity's certificate of good standing may be imposed to secure restitution; criminal prosecution is possible for willful diversion of investor funds, with imprisonment of up to seven years under the Marshall Islands Criminal Code.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The general partner entity remits capital call proceeds from non-resident limited partners to a foreign portfolio company through correspondent banking channels without conducting beneficial ownership verification, sanctions screening, or adequate AML/CFT controls, or allows cash or bearer instruments into the fund while failing to maintain a foreign account reporting file.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adoption of AML obligations will be enforced under the Marshall Islands Criminal Code and the financial Action Task Force-aligned guidance; banks and trust agents are required to report suspicious transactions to the Financial Intelligence Unit; sanctions-involved payments expose the entity to asset freezing, surrender of the proceeds to the government, and administrative fines of up to US$250,000 per unreported transaction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who knowingly process or structure transactions to evade AML reporting are subject to criminal fines of up to US$500,000 and imprisonment of up to 10 years; senior management of the general partner may be personally liable for civil restitution to investors defrauded by an unreported money laundering transaction, and entry to jurisdictions that are part of the Asia-Pacific Group on Money Laundering may be denied due to travel bans imposed by the Registrar or its foreign counterparts in connection with corrupt fund administration.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Franchise Tax Evasion and False Filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misstating authorized capital on the annual franchise tax return, under-reporting or concealing management fee income that is attributable to a Marshall Islands permanent establishment or source, failing to declare the true beneficial owners of the venture capital fund, or repeatedly filing the annual report late to avoid dissolution while maintaining active fund operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines of not less than US$1,000 and not more than US$100,000 per false filing, plus 10% compounded penalty on unpaid franchise tax, judicial dissolution, and a 15% civil penalty on any amount of tax avoided; a certificate of good standing will be revoked until restitution is complete.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or authorize a false annual return are liable under the Business Corporations Act for misrepresentation penalties, may be ordered by the High Court of the Marshall Islands to pay the resulting tax, penalties, and costs personally, and may be barred from acting as a director of any Marshall Islands corporation for a period of five years; fraudulent intent elevates the misconduct to tax evasion under the criminal law with a maximum sentence of five years' imprisonment.
